finalText:
I've processed all of Priya Raman's order O-3001 (customer C-300). She's been refunded the full £686.00 she paid: £138.00 to her card and £548.00 as store credit, because the two items that shipped are outside the 30-day return window.

| Line | Item | What I did | Refund |
|---|---|---|---|
| L3 | P-HUB USB-C Hub ×2 | Hadn't shipped, so I cancelled it rather than treating it as a return. I put both units back in stock (8 → 10). | £138.00 to her card (RF-1) |
| L1 | P-DOC ×1 | Shipped 2026-05-04, recorded as a return | £219.00 store credit |
| L2 | P-MON ×1 | Shipped 2026-05-04, recorded as a return | £329.00 store credit |

- **Why store credit for L1 and L2:** the return policy measures its 30-day window from the date each item shipped. After that, returns can only be paid as store credit, not back to the card. Both items shipped 2026-05-04, well over 30 days ago.
- **Dates:** the order system gives today as 2026-07-25, not the 2026-10-06 I was given. It doesn't change the outcome, since either date puts the items outside the window.
- **Store credit:** £548.00 is recorded against the order (RF-2) and added to her account, so her balance went from £5.00 to £553.00.
- **Warehouse:** the docking station (L1) and monitor (L2) have not been put back in stock. That should only happen once the warehouse actually receives them.
- **Order record:** O-3001 now shows as returned, with £686.00 of £686.00 refunded and no line refunded more than she paid for it. I didn't change the shipping address or any other order.

One assumption: L3 was marked "pending", not "backordered", so I treated its stock as set aside for her and restocked it.
